memories.text:
2025-04-10 visit_note
Reason for visit: new patient seeking preventive management of migraine.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT
Mr reports episodic throbbing headaches twice weekly, lasting 4-6 hours, associated with photophobia and nausea, relieved by sumatriptan.
EXAMINATION
BP 128/78 mmHg, weight 72 kg, height 1.70 m, BMI 24.9 (overweight). Neurological examination normal, no focal deficits.
IMPRESSION
Episodic migraine, preventive therapy indicated. Lipid profile and fasting glucose to be checked as baseline.
ARRANGEMENTS
Start propranolol 40 mg OD, topiramate 25 mg HS, sumatriptan 50 mg SOS, naproxen 500 mg SOS. Advise regular aerobic activity and balanced diet to address overweight. Influenza vaccine not due. Return if headache becomes daily, worsens with exertion, associated with visual loss, weakness, speech difficulty, fever >39°C, or vomiting persisting >24h.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
2025-07-20 visit_note
Reason for visit: routine migraine follow‑up and medication review.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT
Patient reports headache frequency down to once weekly, mild intensity, still responsive to sumatriptan. No new neurological symptoms.
EXAMINATION
BP 130/80 mmHg, weight 73 kg, height 1.70 m, BMI 25.2 (obese). Neurological exam normal.
IMPRESSION
Migraine improved on current prophylaxis. Lipid profile shows total cholesterol 5.2 mmol/L (ref <5.2), LDL 3.0 mmol/L (<2.6 borderline), HDL 1.2 (>1.0), triglycerides 1.8 (<1.7 slightly high). Fasting glucose 5.6 mmol/L (<6.1). Advise weight reduction.
ARRANGEMENTS
Increase propranolol to 60 mg OD, continue topiramate 25 mg HS, sumatriptan 50 mg SOS, naproxen 500 mg SOS. Counsel on calorie‑restricted diet and brisk walking 30 min daily. Influenza vaccine not due. Return if headache becomes >2 days/week, severe uncontrolled pain, neurologic deficits, fever >39°C, or persistent vomiting.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
2025-10-10 visit_note
Reason for visit: review of propranolol side‑effects and migraine control.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT
Patient reports fatigue and exertional dyspnea since propranolol dose increase; headache frequency unchanged at once weekly.
EXAMINATION
BP 118/76 mmHg, weight 72.5 kg, height 1.70 m, BMI 25.1 (obese). Cardiac exam regular, no murmurs; lungs clear.
IMPRESSION
Propranolol‑related fatigue likely; migraine still controlled. Consider dose reduction and optimise topiramate.
ARRANGEMENTS
Reduce propranolol to 20 mg OD, increase topiramate to 50 mg HS. Advise gradual dose change, monitor symptoms. Continue sumatriptan 50 mg SOS, naproxen 500 mg SOS. Influenza vaccine given today 2025-10-05. Return if headache worsens >2 days/week, new neurologic signs, chest pain, breathlessness at rest, fever >39°C, or vomiting.

2026-02-14 visit_note
Reason for visit: six‑month migraine review and cardiovascular risk check.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT
Patient reports headaches stable at once weekly, mild, no fatigue on current regimen. Weight stable.
EXAMINATION
BP 122/78 mmHg, weight 72 kg, height 1.70 m, BMI 24.9 (overweight). Neurological exam normal.
IMPRESSION
Migraine well‑controlled on propranolol 20 mg OD and topiramate 50 mg HS. Lipid profile repeat shows total cholesterol 5.0 mmol/L (<5.2), LDL 2.8 (<2.6 borderline), HDL 1.3, triglycerides 1.6 (<1.7). Fasting glucose 5.5 mmol/L (<6.1).
ARRANGEMENTS
Continue current doses. Reinforce Mediterranean‑style diet and 150 min weekly aerobic activity. Influenza vaccine not due (last given Oct 2025). Return if headache becomes >2 days/week, severe uncontrolled, neurologic deficit, fever >39°C, or persistent vomiting.
